input:
/app/app.db is a schema version 1 SQLite database created from /app/schema_v1.sql. Write the migration /app/migrations/002_users_v2.sql and apply it to /app/app.db with `sqlite3 /app/app.db < /app/migrations/002_users_v2.sql`. The file must be plain SQL that upgrades ANY version 1 database (it will also be run against other v1 databases with different rows).

Version 2:
- users has exactly the columns (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT NOT NULL, last_name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL), in that order, keeping user ids.
- From full_name with surrounding spaces trimmed: first_name is the text before the first space, last_name the rest with surrounding spaces trimmed ('' when there is no space).
- email is trimmed and lowercased. Users whose emails are equal after that are merged: keep only the lowest id, and orders of the removed users now belong to the kept user.
- signup (MM/DD/YYYY) becomes signup_date YYYY-MM-DD.
- meta schema_version is '2'.
orders keeps its columns and rows (only user_id may change).

transcript.final_response:
Migration complete.

**`/app/migrations/002_users_v2.sql`** (plain SQL, works on any v1 DB):
1. Reassigns `orders.user_id` to `MIN(id)` per normalized email (`lower(trim(email))`), guarded so orphan `user_id`s are untouched.
2. Deletes duplicate users, keeping lowest `id` per normalized email.
3. Rebuilds `users` as `(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT NOT NULL, last_name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL)` in that order, preserving ids, with:
   - `first_name` = text before first space of `trim(full_name)`, `last_name` = trimmed remainder (`''` if no space)
   - `email` = `lower(trim(email))`
   - `signup_date` = `MM/DD/YYYY` → `YYYY-MM-DD` via `printf('%04d-%02d-%02d',…)` (handles non-zero-padded and padded dates)
4. Sets `meta.schema_version` to `'2'`.

Applied via `sqlite3 /app/app.db < /app/migrations/002_users_v2.sql`. Verified on `/app/app.db` (Ada duplicate merged: users 1,2,3,5 kept; orders 101,104 → user 1) and on an edge-case v1 DB (multi-space names, single-word names, 3-way email dupes, dangling order).
tool_calls:
cat /app/schema_v1.sql; echo "---"; ls -R /app; echo "---"; cat /app/app.db 2>&1 | head -c 500; echo
sqlite3 /app/app.db ".tables" 2>&1
sqlite3 /app/app.db ".schema" 2>&1
sqlite3 /app/app.db "SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 20;" 2>&1
sqlite3 /app/app.db "SELECT * FROM orders LIMIT 20;" 2>&1
sqlite3 /app/app.db "SELECT * FROM meta;" 2>&1

sqlite3 --version; sqlite3 /app/app.db "SELECT sqlite_version();"
ls -la /app/migrations/ 2>&1 || echo "no migrations dir"

cp /app/app.db /tmp/app_backup.db
sqlite3 /app/app.db < /app/migrations/002_users_v2.sql
echo "exit=$?"
echo "--- schema ---"
sqlite3 /app/app.db ".schema users"
sqlite3 /app/app.db ".schema orders"
sqlite3 /app/app.db ".schema meta"
echo "--- PRAGMA table_info ---"
sqlite3 /app/app.db "PRAGMA table_info(users);"
echo "--- users ---"
sqlite3 /app/app.db "SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY id;"
echo "--- orders ---"
sqlite3 /app/app.db "SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY id;"
echo "--- meta ---"
sqlite3 /app/app.db "SELECT * FROM meta;"

ls -la /app/ /app/migrations/
echo "=== final app.db state ==="
sqlite3 /app/app.db "SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY id; SELECT '---'; SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY id; SELECT '---'; SELECT * FROM meta;"
echo "=== verify counts ==="
sqlite3 /app/app.db "SELECT count(*) FROM users; SELECT count(*) FROM orders;"
rm -f /tmp/test_v1.db /tmp/app_backup.db
